home.subtitle: Hernando Rojas Rentería
home.title: "CHALO"
home.description: From Cali, Chalo Rojas has spent more than five decades drawing, painting, and making photographs. From everyday interiors to abstraction, his work is driven by the same curiosity: to look again at what is right in front of us.
home.trajectoryTitle: More than five decades of creation
home.trajectoryText: I entered Cali's School of Fine Arts at fourteen. In 1977, I received first prize for drawing at the National Salon of Young Artists at La Tertulia. Since then, I have exhibited in Colombia and abroad and shared my practice as a teacher.
home.paintingsText: Decades of pictorial exploration condensed on canvas. Each work is a fragment of a world seen through the eyes of someone who never stopped looking.
home.sketchesText: Figures, animals, and invented worlds in small format. Free line, direct color, the urgency of the gesture.
home.photosText: Decades walking the streets of Cali with a camera. Architecture, memory, and light in black and white.
home.ctaText: Write to me to ask about my works or if you want to learn about my creative process.

biografia.label: TRAJECTORY
biografia.title: Biography
biografia.bio_p1: Hernando ‘Chalo’ Rojas Rentería was born in Cali in 1950 and grew up in the El Cedro neighborhood, surrounded by books, conversation, and streets he learned to observe as a child. At fourteen, he entered Cali's School of Fine Arts to pursue a calling already evident in his drawings.
biografia.bio_p2: He also trained in graphic design at SENA and studied photography in Cali and New York. One of his earliest works was a drawing of a kitchen filled with pots, spoons, and calendars. That attention to interiors and everyday objects, to light and shadow, accompanied his move toward abstraction.
biografia.bio_p3: In 1977, he won first prize for drawing at the National Salon of Young Artists at Museo La Tertulia. He then spent ten years at Corporación Prográfica, deepening his knowledge of graphic arts alongside Pedro Alcántara Herrán and the work of artists from Colombia and across the Americas.
biografia.bio_p4: His first exhibition was in 1969, alongside fellow Fine Arts students. His work was later shown across Colombia and in the United States, Puerto Rico, Cuba, Ecuador, Norway, Panama, and Switzerland. In 2000, he showed his photographs at the Instituto Hispanoamericano in Berlin, his most important exhibition.
biografia.bio_p5: He has also taught at Universidad del Cauca, Universidad Autónoma de Occidente, and Instituto Popular de Cultura. He continues to draw, paint, and photograph with a curiosity he sums up in one line: ‘The more I live, the more I see, and the more I will create.’
